svg.title: 99.44% recovered from a real kill -- against 0% for the plain dict this exact scenario broke
svg.desc: A Faust table aggregating revenue by zone across 15,000 real trips. Run 1 processes the full topic and its live total, $388,422.49, exactly matches the ground truth computed independently in plain Python. The worker is killed with SIGKILL. Run 2 starts a fresh process with zero new messages to consume -- Kafka's offsets are already at the end -- and the table recovers $386,244.66 from its own changelog topic on startup, 99.44% of the true total, compared to the plain consumer loop from Lesson 1 which recovered exactly 0%.
svg.text: A Real SIGKILL, and What Actually Comes Back
exact match to ground truth -- then SIGKILL
recovered from the changelog on startup alone
99.44% recovered -- vs 0.00% for Lesson 1's plain dict
the missing 0.56% is one update whose changelog write hadn't landed when SIGKILL arrived --
durability for completed writes, not atomicity with the in-memory update
This is the exact gap Lesson 1 proved exists -- now measured, closed, and explained
